decisions.reason: The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY locking the accent as an exact Hero V right-arm copy with identical peak height and terminal geometry; no additional update or removal is required.
The accent peak-alignment revision policy does not change the second V hierarchy, which already has its own same-message lock policy.

The Hero V remains the fixed alignment reference, and its same-message MODIFY already preserves its master geometry and agreed elevation; the accent alignment policy adds no further Hero V state change.
Exact Hero V-to-accent peak alignment does not alter the second V glyph geometry; its proportional derivation and terminal propagation rules are already represented by a same-message MODIFY.

Peak alignment is independently owned by the source Requirement, while the candidate's same-message MODIFY already captures terminal exploration and propagation without requiring an additional alignment attribute.
Locking the Hero V and É accent peak relationship does not change the architectural construction or originality requirements for the E and L letterforms.
The geometric peak-alignment policy does not change the selected champagne finish, color distribution, or material-treatment constraints.
Preserving Hero V-to-accent peak alignment does not alter the selected Balanced Flow kerning or cohesive-reading requirement.
The source concerns top-peak alignment between the Hero V and É accent, not the existing bottom-baseline alignment of the wordmark.
The Hero V-to-accent peak lock does not change the E/L cap-height rule based on the second V's left arm.
The geometric alignment policy has no effect on the separate obligation to explain design intentions and their translation into letterforms.

The source message separately introduces the presentation protocol, and that requirement already has its own same-message INTRODUCE; the alignment-policy MODIFY requires no additional propagated event.
